items.stem: What news does Ismene bring?
options: The sons are fighting over Thebes and Creon is coming for Oedipus
Thebes has already fallen to a foreign army from across the sea
Theseus lies dead, and Athens is left without any king at all
The sacred grove at Colonus has been burned down to the ground

items.stem: What does Theseus grant Oedipus?
options: Protection in Athens
A throne in place of his old one
An army to march back on Thebes
A new name to hide his past life

items.stem: Complete Ismene's account of the brothers: “Have stirred betwixt them a mad _____”
options: alliance
silence
rivalry
treaty

items.stem: Complete the chorus's instruction: “Make a _____ first of water fetched”
options: fortress
banquet
sermon
libation

items.stem: Why do the Thebans now want Oedipus?
options: An oracle says whoever holds his grave will prosper
They want to punish him a second time in public court
They want to set him on the Theban throne again today
They need his money to pay a hired foreign army

items.stem: Why does Theseus understand Oedipus?
options: He too was raised in exile
He is Oedipus's long-lost younger son
He is himself blind and led by a child
He was born and reared in Thebes himself

items.stem: How does Oedipus defend himself?
options: He acted in self-defence and without knowledge
He puts the whole blame for the past on Antigone alone
He denies that any killing ever took place at all
He says that Creon struck Laius on the public road

items.stem: Who brings Oedipus the news from Thebes in this episode?
options: Ismene
Antigone
Creon of Thebes
King Theseus

items.stem: How does the chorus say Oedipus must speak the prayer of the rite?
options: In whispered accents, not with lifted voice
With a loud cry already heard in Thebes
In a song already taught by Creon
In silence, without any words at all

items.stem: Complete the oracle as Ismene reports it: “To have thee for their _____ alive or dead.”
options: burden
weal
exile
ransom

items.stem: Complete the chorus's first instruction: “First make _____ to the deities,”
options: accusation
festival
bargain
atonement

items.stem: According to Ismene, what did Oedipus's sons know and still set aside?
options: The oracle about him, outweighed by their greed of rule
That Theseus had already promised him a Theban throne that day
That Antigone had refused to stay and help their father
That the grove at Colonus had already been wholly destroyed

items.stem: Why, according to Ismene, will the Thebans not actually shroud Oedipus's bones in Theban dust?
options: Guilt of a kinsman's blood forbids that burial
They have already built him a tomb in Argos
Phoebus has forbidden any tomb for him at all
Theseus has claimed the body as an Athenian prize

items.stem: What is the point of Theseus's claim, “I too was reared, / Like thee, in exile”?
options: Shared exile is the ground on which he offers welcome
He is proving that Oedipus was not a Theban by birth
He wants Oedipus to return with him at once to Thebes
He is warning that Athens also means to drive him out

items.stem: Who does the chorus announce as sovereign of Athens in this episode?
options: Theseus, the son of Aegeus
Creon, coming in haste from Thebes
Polyneices, reported as still waiting in Argos
A nameless guardian of the sacred close

items.stem: Complete Ismene's line: “The gods, who once _____, uplift thee now.”
options: exalted
abased
ignored
rewarded

items.stem: Complete Theseus's grant: “But grant him the full rights of _____,”
options: prisoner
messenger
servant
citizen

items.stem: What does Oedipus say Theseus will gain, and when will that gain appear?
options: The worth of his burial, once Theseus has buried him
An immediate victory over Argos in the next battle
The Theban throne, transferred to Athens that day
A cure for blindness, granted as soon as he is housed

items.stem: Why does Oedipus pray that his sons' feud never be quenched?
options: They did nothing to help him when he was banned and banished
They tried to make him king of Colonus against his will
They asked Ismene to keep the Theban throne in their name
They refused to let Ismene leave Thebes in order to find him

items.stem: When the elders charge Oedipus with sin, he answers, “I sinnèd not.” What does that reply claim?
options: He denies that the suffering came from acts done in malice
He denies that Laius ever died on the road at all that day
He claims the chorus has no right to ask him any question
He says Ismene, not he, should answer for the whole past

items.stem: Complete Oedipus's warning: “There is no _____ ’twixt friend and friend,”
options: enmity
constancy
silence
distance

items.stem: Complete Ismene's prophecy: “Thy angry _____, when at thy tomb they stand.”
options: blessing
armor
wraith
scepter

items.stem: What does Theseus mean by “An oath would be no surer than my word”?
options: He treats his spoken pledge as already binding, without a further oath
He is refusing to protect Oedipus until a formal oath is sworn first
He wants Oedipus to swear first before Athens will offer any help
He believes oracles are already surer than any human spoken promise

items.stem: What is the force of Oedipus's phrase “a man more sinned against than sinning”?
options: It asks the elders to weigh what was done to him above what he did
It admits that his sins were greater than any wrong he had suffered
It claims that no person in Thebes ever committed any sin at all
It tells the chorus that only Theseus may judge a fallen king

items.stem: In Oedipus's speech about his children, how does he contrast the daughters with the sons?
options: The daughters gave care and harbourage; the sons sacrificed him for power
The daughters fled to Argos, while the sons remained behind to nurse him
The sons brought food, but the daughters tried to seize the Theban throne
Both pairs of children, in this speech, refused him any kind of help at all

items.stem: Which statement best captures how this episode recasts Oedipus's position?
options: The outcast becomes a treasure a city may want to keep and protect
Theseus drives him out as soon as the Theban oracle is first heard
Oedipus recovers his sight and returns to rule in Thebes at once
The sons send peaceful gifts and ask him to bless all of their rule
